questions.stem: Why do you talk about the client's lifestyle during a haircut consultation?
options: To decide how much more to charge for the cut
So you can tell her about your own weekend
To find out which salon she used to go to before
So the cut suits the time she has to style it

questions.stem: What is a cowlick?
options: A tuft of hair growing in a different direction
A bald patch on the scalp caused by very tight braids
A type of split end that is found on long, dry hair
A short, heavy fringe that is cut straight across

questions.stem: Why do you check for a double crown before cutting short hair?
options: It means the client needs a perm to make it lie flat
It shows that the client has a scalp infection
Cutting too short there can make the hair stick up
It tells you to use a razor instead of scissors

questions.stem: During the consultation you see head lice eggs (nits) in Andre's hair. What should you do?
options: Cut the hair very short so that the lice are removed
Cut the hair and then spray it with disinfectant
Do not cut; tell him politely and advise treatment
Cut it quickly and wash the tools at the end of the day

questions.stem: Which scalp condition means you should not cut the hair, and should refer the client to a doctor?
options: Dandruff, with small dry white flakes
Natural grey hair at the temples
A dry scalp after the sun
Ringworm, with round scaly patches

questions.stem: What is the parietal ridge?
options: The bone that sticks out at the back, near the nape
The highest point on the top of the head
The line where the hair meets the forehead
The widest part of the head, around the top sides

questions.stem: What is the occipital bone?
options: The bone just above the eyebrows, at the very front
The bone that sticks out at the back of the head
The flat bone at the very top of the crown area
The small bone found just in front of each ear

questions.stem: In hair shaping, what is elevation?
options: How high the client's chair is raised for the cut
How sharp the blades of the scissors are
How wet the hair is kept while it is cut
The angle the hair is lifted from the head

questions.stem: Which elevation gives a one-length (blunt) cut?
options: 45 degrees
90 degrees
0 degrees
180 degrees

questions.stem: Which elevation is used for a uniform layer cut, where all the hair is about the same length?
options: 0 degrees
90 degrees
45 degrees
15 degrees

questions.stem: What does a graduated cut, using about 45 degrees of elevation, create?
options: A build-up of weight, stacking up from the nape
Long, even layers all over the head with no weight at all
A single hanging length with a heavy line at the bottom
Very short hair all over the head, all the same length

questions.stem: What is a guideline in hair cutting?
options: A line drawn on the salon floor to show where to stand
The first section of hair that is washed at the basin
A note written on the record card about the client's style
The first cut section that sets the length for the rest

questions.stem: What is the difference between a stationary guide and a travelling guide?
options: A stationary guide is cut wet; a travelling guide is cut dry
A stationary guide is used only on men; a travelling guide only on women
A travelling guide is used only with clippers
All hair goes to a stationary guide; a travelling guide moves with you

questions.stem: Why should you use little tension when cutting curly hair wet?
options: Curly hair shrinks as it dries, so it can end up too short
Curly hair is much stronger, so no tension at all is needed
Tension on wet hair makes the scissor blades go blunt faster
Too little tension on wet hair makes the natural curls drop

questions.stem: Why do many stylists shape natural coily hair when it is dry and picked out?
options: They can see the true shape and length after shrinkage
Dry hair is a lot easier to sweep up from the floor
Wet coily hair cannot be cut with any scissors at all
Picked-out hair needs no sectioning or checking at all

questions.stem: What are thinning (texturising) scissors mainly used for?
options: Cutting a strong, straight guideline at the nape
Removing bulk without changing the length much
Cutting a neat, sharp outline around the ears
Trimming the client's eyebrows and beard

questions.stem: On which hair should a razor usually not be used?
options: Dry or very curly hair, because it can fray and frizz
Wet, straight hair that needs soft, tapered ends on it
Hair on a practice head during training
Fine hair that is cut wet

questions.stem: What are clipper attachment combs (guards) used for?
options: To clean the hair out of the blades
To cool the blades while the clipper is running
To hold the client's ear out of the way
To leave the hair at a set, even length

questions.stem: What is 'point cutting'?
options: Cutting into the ends with the tips to soften the line
Cutting the hair straight across to a point at the nape
Cutting the hair while pointing the scissors at the floor
Cutting a pointed fringe in the middle of the forehead

questions.stem: How should clippers be cared for between clients?
options: Brush off hair, then disinfect and oil as the maker says
Dip the running clipper head into a bowl of soapy water
Leave them plugged in and lying on the chair, ready to use
Wipe them with the client's used towel and put them in a drawer

questions.stem: How should you hold the scissors while combing the hair between cuts?
options: Open, with the blades pointing towards the client
Closed and palmed (held in the palm of the hand)
Held in your mouth, so that both hands are free
Balanced on the client's shoulder until needed

questions.stem: How should you pass scissors to another person?
options: Toss them gently so that they land on the trolley
Closed, with the handles towards the other person
Open, with the blade points towards the other person
Slide them across the floor with your foot

questions.stem: What should you do with a used razor blade?
options: Wrap it in tissue and put it in the normal bin
Rinse it and keep it for the next client
Put it in a sharps box, because it is single-use
Leave it on the trolley until the end of the day

options: So that the client can take her hair home with her
Because cut hair changes colour if it is left on the floor

questions.stem: Before using electric clippers, what should you check?
options: The cord, plug and blades are in good order
That the clipper is still warm from the last client
That the guard has been taken off, so the cut is closer
That the clipper is plugged in right next to the wet basin

questions.stem: You nick a client's ear and it bleeds a little. What should you do first?
options: Carry on cutting and clean it up at the end
Put on gloves and press a clean pad on the cut
Spray it with hair spray to stop the bleeding
Ask the client to hold a tissue on it while you finish

questions.stem: Why is a neck strip put on before the cape?
options: To keep the client's head and neck warm in the salon
To stop the cape from slipping off the shoulders
To soak up the water from the spray bottle
To stop the cape touching the skin and keep hair out

questions.stem: How should the client sit for a haircut?
options: With legs crossed and head turned to one side
Upright, with feet flat and legs uncrossed
Leaning back with the head on the basin
Slouched down so that the stylist can reach

questions.stem: Why do you section the hair before cutting?
options: To make the haircut take a little longer
To make the client's hair dry much faster
To control the hair and cut in a set order
To show the client where the hair is thinnest

questions.stem: Why do you keep straight hair evenly damp while you wet-cut it?
options: Hair that dries as you cut can end up uneven
Damp hair makes the scissors cut more sharply
Dry straight hair can never be cut with any scissors
Water on the hair makes it grow back much more slowly

questions.stem: What is over-direction?
options: Cutting more hair off than the client wanted
Cutting with the client's head bent too far forward
Combing hair away from its natural fall to a guide
Using two guidelines at the same time

questions.stem: Why should the client's head be kept upright (not tilted) while you cut a one-length bob?
options: To stop the client from falling asleep in the chair
So the client can watch television
So that the hair dries evenly
A tilted head makes the line come out uneven

questions.stem: What is cross-checking a haircut?
options: Asking another stylist to come and finish the cut
Checking the price list before the client pays for it
Taking sections the opposite way to check the lines
Combing the hair forward to see the fringe

questions.stem: How do you check that both sides of a haircut are even?
options: Ask the client to feel the ends with her eyes closed
Measure each side with a tape after the client leaves
Compare the same points on each side in the mirror
Look at the hair on the floor on each side

questions.stem: When shaping a rounded afro, why is the hair lifted out evenly with a pick first?
options: So the shape is even before you trim it
To make the hair shrink back before cutting
To straighten the coils of the hair for good
To remove the natural oils from the scalp

questions.stem: Rohan wants a taper on his short natural hair. What does a taper mean?
options: The hair is shortest at the nape and gets longer going up
The hair is cut to exactly the same length all over the head
The hair is longest at the nape and shortest up on top
A thin line shaved into the side of the hair as a design

questions.stem: Why may textured hair look shorter after it dries than when it was cut wet?
options: The scissors cut off more than you could see
Curls and coils shrink up as they dry
The hair breaks off as it dries
The dryer burns off the ends

questions.stem: Shelly-Ann has a round face. Which style usually suits her best?
options: Very full, wide sides at cheek level
Some height on top, with less width at the sides
A short, heavy, straight fringe
A centre parting with all the volume at the jaw

questions.stem: After the cut, how should loose hair be removed from the client's neck and face?
options: Blow it off with your mouth
Wipe it off with a wet hand
Brush it off with a clean neck brush
Leave it for the client to remove at home

questions.stem: Which step completes a haircut service?
options: Sending the client away with damp hair and cut hair on her neck
Selling her the most expensive product in the salon
Booking her next visit for one year later
Styling, showing her the back in a mirror and agreeing the result

questions.stem: How should combs be made safe for the next client?
options: Run them under the tap and put them in your pocket
Remove hair, wash them, then disinfect them
Wipe them on the cape and use them again
Leave them in the disinfectant with hair on them

questions.stem: Why must hair be removed from a tool before it goes into disinfectant?
options: Disinfectant makes the hair stick hard to the tool
Disinfectant cannot work properly through dirt and hair
Hair in the jar makes the disinfectant smell very bad
Hair in the jar turns the disinfectant into plain water

questions.stem: How often would you usually advise a client to come back to keep the shape of a short cut?
options: Once every year
Only when the hair reaches her shoulders
Every few weeks, as suits the style
Every day for the first week

questions.stem: Why should you adjust the height of the client's chair?
options: So that the client can see out of the salon window
So that the client can rest her feet up on the trolley
So the hair falls to the floor faster
So you can work with a straight back and good view

questions.stem: Your scissors start to fold the hair instead of cutting cleanly. What should you do?
options: Push harder on the handles so that they cut
Cut wetter hair to help them

essays.stem: Describe what you would discuss and check during a consultation before a haircut.
essays.modelAnswer: I greet the client, gown her, and ask what she wants, using pictures so that we agree on the length and shape. I ask how much time she spends on her hair each day, about her work and sports, and what products and tools she uses at home. I look at her face shape and head shape, and I check the hair's texture, density, curl pattern and condition, wet and dry if needed. I look for growth patterns such as a cowlick, a widow's peak, a whorl or a double crown, because they affect how short I can cut. I check the scalp for cuts, lice, ringworm or other infections; if I find any, I do not cut and politely advise her to get treatment. Then I explain what I plan to do, tell her the price and time, agree it, and write it on the record card.
markingPoints: Agrees the length and shape wanted, using pictures
Asks about lifestyle, styling time and home care
Checks face shape, texture, density, curl pattern and condition
Checks growth patterns (cowlick, widow's peak, whorl, double crown)
Checks the scalp for contraindications, and agrees price and time; records it

essays.stem: Explain what elevation is, and describe the effect of cutting at 0, 45, 90 and 180 degrees.
essays.modelAnswer: Elevation is the angle at which the hair is lifted away from the head before it is cut. It controls where the weight and the layers fall. At 0 degrees, the hair is combed down flat in its natural fall and cut. All the hair ends at one length, so it gives a one-length or blunt cut with a strong weight line, such as a bob. At about 45 degrees, the hair is lifted a little. This gives a graduated cut, where the hair is short at the nape and stacks up into a build-up of weight. At 90 degrees, the hair is held straight out from the curve of the head. This gives uniform layers, where all the hair is about the same length. At 180 degrees, the hair is held straight up from the top of the head. This gives long layers: short on top and longer underneath.
markingPoints: Elevation is the angle the hair is lifted from the head
0 degrees: one-length (blunt) cut with a strong weight line
45 degrees: graduation, building weight from the nape
90 degrees: uniform layers, all about the same length
180 degrees: long layers, short on top and longer underneath

essays.stem: Describe the main tools used in hair shaping, and say what each one is used for.
essays.modelAnswer: Scissors (shears) are the main cutting tool. They are used for blunt cutting, layering, point cutting and slide cutting. Thinning or texturising scissors have teeth on one or both blades, and remove bulk without taking off much length. A razor is used on wet straight hair to give soft, tapered ends; it is not used on dry or very curly hair, because it can make it fray. Clippers cut short hair, and their attachment combs (guards) leave the hair at a set length, which is useful for tapers on natural hair. Trimmers make sharp outlines around the hairline and ears. A cutting comb has fine teeth for straight hair and wide teeth for curly hair, and a pick is used to lift out natural hair. Sectioning clips hold the hair out of the way, a water spray keeps it damp, and a neck brush removes cut hair from the skin.
markingPoints: Scissors for main cutting; thinning scissors to remove bulk
Razor on wet straight hair only, for soft ends
Clippers with guards for set lengths and tapers; trimmers for outlines
Cutting comb (fine and wide teeth) and pick for natural hair
Clips, water spray and neck brush, with their uses

essays.stem: Describe how you would use, carry and store scissors, razors and clippers safely in the salon.
essays.modelAnswer: I keep scissors closed when I am not cutting, and I palm them while I comb, so the blades are not open near the client's face and ears. I pass them closed, with the handles towards the other person, and I never carry them in my pocket. I store them in a case or a clean drawer. A razor always has a guard or a new blade, and I use it with care on wet hair only. Used blades are single-use: they go straight into a sharps box. Before using clippers, I check that the cord, plug and blades are in good order and that my hands are dry, and I keep them away from water. I switch them off and unplug them when I am not using them. I fold the ear down and hold it when cutting near it. If a tool is damaged or blunt, I stop using it and report it.
markingPoints: Scissors closed and palmed when not cutting; passed handles first; stored in a case
Razor guarded, used with care; used blades into a sharps box
Checks clipper cord, plug and blades; dry hands; away from water; unplugged after use
Protects the ears and face while cutting
Stops using and reports damaged or blunt tools

essays.stem: Describe the steps for cutting a one-length (blunt) bob on straight or relaxed hair, from sectioning to checking.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation, I shampoo the hair and comb it smooth, then sit the client upright with her feet flat and her head level. I divide the hair into four sections and clip the top away. Starting at the nape, I take a thin horizontal section, comb it straight down with no elevation (0 degrees) and little tension, and cut the guideline to the agreed length, checking that it is straight and even. I bring down the next section, comb it over the guide, and cut it to the same line. I keep going up the back, then do the sides, bringing the side hair to the back guide so that the line joins. I keep the hair evenly damp and the client's head upright. At the end I check the line in the mirror on both sides, cross-check, and dry the hair to check the line again, then refine it.
markingPoints: Client upright with the head level; hair sectioned
Cuts a nape guideline at 0 degrees with little tension
Brings each section down to the stationary guide and cuts to the same line
Joins the sides to the back guide; keeps the hair damp
Checks both sides in the mirror, cross-checks and refines when dry

essays.stem: Explain how you would shape natural coily hair, and why shrinkage and tension matter.
essays.modelAnswer: Natural coily hair shrinks a great deal when it dries, so wet hair that is stretched and cut can end up much shorter than the client wanted. For that reason, I cut with very little tension, and I often shape the hair dry, in its natural state, so that I can see the true length and shape. First I check the scalp and detangle the hair gently from the ends upwards with a wide-tooth comb or pick. For a rounded afro, I lift the hair out evenly with a pick, then trim it into an even shape with scissors, working round the head and stepping back often to check the outline. For a short taper, I use clippers with guards, shortest at the nape and longer going up, and I blend it with scissor-over-comb. I outline the hairline with trimmers, and I take care not to cut too short over growth patterns.
markingPoints: Coily hair shrinks when dry, so stretched wet hair ends up shorter
Uses very little tension and often shapes the hair dry
Detangles gently from the ends with a wide-tooth comb or pick
Picks out evenly and trims the shape, checking the outline often
Uses clipper guards and scissor-over-comb for tapers; outlines with trimmers

essays.stem: Explain how you would keep the tools, towels and workstation hygienic between haircut clients. Include the difference between cleaning and disinfecting.
essays.modelAnswer: Cleaning means removing hair, dirt and product with soap and water, and it must always come first, because disinfectant cannot work through hair and dirt. Disinfecting means using a chemical, made up and timed as the maker says, to kill most germs on a cleaned item. After each client, I remove the hair from my combs and brushes, wash them, then put them in disinfectant for the maker's time and dry them. I wipe my scissors clean and disinfect them as the maker says. I brush the hair out of the clipper blades, then spray them with a clipper disinfectant and oil them. Razor blades go in the sharps box. Each client has a fresh towel and neck strip, and used towels go in the laundry. I sweep up cut hair, wipe the chair and trolley with disinfectant, and wash my hands before the next client.
markingPoints: Cleaning removes hair and dirt and must come first
Disinfecting kills most germs, using the maker's strength and time
Combs washed then disinfected; scissors and clippers cleaned, disinfected and oiled
Used blades in a sharps box; fresh towel and neck strip for each client
Sweeps hair, wipes surfaces and washes hands

essays.stem: Describe how you would check a haircut for balance and accuracy before you finish.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the cut as I go and again at the end. First I cross-check: I take sections in the opposite direction to the ones I cut with, for example vertical sections if I cut with horizontal ones, and I hold them at the same elevation to see that the lines and layers are even. I look in the mirror and compare the same points on each side, such as the length at the ears, the cheekbones and the jaw. I check that the weight line or graduation is smooth, with no steps or holes. For a natural cut, I step back and check the shape from the front, sides and back, picking the hair out again where needed. I check the neckline and outline are clean. Then I dry and style the hair, because hair can look different when dry, and I make small corrections. Last, I show the client the back with a hand mirror.
markingPoints: Cross-checks with sections in the opposite direction
Compares the same points on each side in the mirror
Checks the weight line, layers or shape for steps or holes
Checks the outline and neckline
Dries, re-checks and refines, then shows the client the back

essays.stem: Describe the conditions that mean you should not cut a client's hair, and what you would do if you cut a client by accident.
essays.modelAnswer: I should not cut if the client has head lice or nits, ringworm (round, scaly patches), impetigo (weeping, crusty sores), or any open wound or infected area on the scalp or neck. These can spread to other people through tools and towels, or get worse. I tell the client politely and in private, advise her to see a doctor or pharmacist, and book her back when it has cleared. I then clean and disinfect all the tools and the area. If I cut a client by accident, I stop at once and stay calm. I put on gloves and press a clean pad or tissue firmly on the cut until the bleeding stops, then cover it with a plaster if she agrees. I tell the instructor and write it in the accident book. Any tool with blood on it is cleaned and disinfected before it is used again.
markingPoints: Names contraindications: lice, ringworm, impetigo, open wounds or infection
Explains they can spread or get worse
Tells the client privately, refers her, and rebooks; disinfects tools
For a cut: gloves, firm pressure with a clean pad, cover it
Reports to the instructor, records it, and disinfects the tool

essays.stem: Compare a graduated cut with a uniform layer cut. Describe the elevation, the guideline and the shape each one gives.
essays.modelAnswer: A graduated cut is cut with low to medium elevation, about 45 degrees. The hair at the nape is shortest, and each section above is a little longer, so the ends stack on top of each other. This builds weight and gives a rounded, stacked shape, often at the back of a bob. It is usually cut with a stationary or a travelling guide, starting at the nape. A uniform layer cut is cut at 90 degrees, with each section held straight out from the curve of the head. All the hair ends up about the same length, so there is no build-up of weight, and the shape follows the round shape of the head. It is cut with a travelling guide that moves from section to section around the head. Graduation suits clients who want weight and shape at the back; uniform layers suit those who want even movement all over.
markingPoints: Graduation: about 45 degrees, short at the nape getting longer
Graduation: builds weight in a stacked, rounded shape
Uniform layers: 90 degrees from the head, all about the same length
Uniform layers: no weight build-up; shape follows the head
Describes the guide used for each and who each suits

practical1.title: One-length bob and uniform layer cut on practice heads
practical1.brief: As a group, set up a clean, safe cutting station and cut two practice (mannequin) heads with damp hair. On the first head, cut a one-length bob at 0 degrees with a stationary guide at the nape. On the second head, cut a uniform layer cut at 90 degrees with a travelling guide. Plan the order together and agree who cuts which part. On the bob, one member cuts the nape guideline and each other member cuts one section up the back or one side, bringing the hair to the guide. On the layer cut, each member cuts at least two sections while the assessor watches. Every member also cross-checks one area and shows the assessor how to hold and pass scissors safely. Photograph each stage below (hair only) and add the photos to the group's practical. Clean and disinfect the tools, sweep up, and hand in once for the whole group.
materials: 2 practice heads with hair at least 20 cm long, on clamps
Disinfectant for tools, as the Centre uses
Broom, dustpan and bin for hair
photos: The cutting station set up, with tools clean and laid out
The bob head sectioned, with the nape guideline cut
The finished bob from the back and each side
The layer head with the first travelling guide held at 90 degrees
The finished layer cut from the back and each side
The station cleaned, hair swept up and tools in the disinfectant
checklist: Sectioned the hair cleanly and kept it under control with clips
Held the hair at the correct elevation for each cut (0 and 90 degrees)
Followed the guideline correctly with even tension
Kept the hair evenly damp and the head upright
Palmed the scissors while combing and passed them safely
Cross-checked and corrected any uneven areas
Cleaned and disinfected tools, swept up hair and left the station tidy
safety: Keep scissors closed and palmed when not cutting; never carry them in a pocket
Sweep up cut hair and wipe up water at once so nobody slips
Clamp the practice heads firmly so they cannot fall
Stand with a straight back and adjust the height of the head

practical2.title: Tapered cut on short natural hair, using clippers, scissor-over-comb and trimmers
practical2.brief: As a group, give a tapered cut on short natural coily hair, on a model who agrees to it or on a practice head with textured hair. Share the work: one member leads the consultation, checks the scalp and growth patterns, and fills in the record card; one detangles the hair gently from the ends and picks it out evenly; then each member cuts part of the head while the assessor watches. One sets the length on top with scissors; others taper the back and the two sides with clippers and guards, shortest at the nape and longer going up; one blends with scissor-over-comb; one makes the outline with trimmers. Every member cross-checks the balance of one area and helps to clean the clippers. Photograph each stage below, showing the hair and head shape only, never the face unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group with the record card.
materials: A model who agrees, or a practice head with short textured hair
Clippers with a set of attachment guards, and trimmers
Cutting scissors, cutting comb, wide-tooth comb and pick
Capes, neck strips, towels and neck brush
Clipper disinfectant spray and clipper oil, as the maker says
photos: The hair picked out evenly before cutting
The top length set with scissors
The back tapered with clippers and guards
The finished cut and outline from the back and both sides
The clippers cleaned, disinfected and oiled, and the area swept
checklist: Checked the scalp and growth patterns before cutting
Detangled and picked out the hair gently, from the ends
Checked the clipper cord, plug and blades and worked with dry hands
Chose the correct guard and tapered evenly from short to longer
Blended the taper smoothly with scissor-over-comb
Cut a clean, even outline with trimmers without cutting the skin
Cross-checked the balance and showed the client the result
Cleaned, disinfected and oiled the clippers and swept up hair
safety: Check electric tools before use; keep them away from water and unplug them after use
Fold and protect the ears when working near them
Do not cut if the scalp has lice, ringworm, sores or open cuts
Sweep up hair at once so nobody slips
